section_plan.title: Conclusion: Repaying the Ethical Debt
section_plan.thesis: The Ethical Debt is real, measurable, and self-reinforcing, but it is repayable. FAIR stewardship, data reuse and virtual control groups, and disciplined stewardship of NAM-generated data each break the loop, provided incentive and governance reform make stewardship count. The strongest ethical claim of the review is also its simplest: because animals paid for the data with their lives, letting the data go to waste is a welfare harm, and repaying the debt saves animals. Key questions remain empirically open.

figure_specs.label: fig:sec09-repayment-roadmap
figure_specs.argument_supported: Synthesises the four repayment mechanisms and their governance/incentive gating into a single pathway, and marks the unresolved empirical questions.
figure_specs.what_it_reveals: Integrates FAIR, reuse/VCG, NAM stewardship, and incentive/governance reform into one diagram keyed to the debt cycle of Figure 1, showing how the parts combine and where evidence is still missing - a synthesis text cannot hold in view at once.
figure_specs.caption_draft: Figure 24. Repaying the Ethical Debt: an integrated pathway. The repayment mechanisms - FAIR stewardship (sec-fair-preclinical), data reuse and virtual control groups (sec-virtual-controls), and stewardship of NAM-generated data (sec-nams-data) - converge on reduced animal use, gated by incentive and governance reform (sec-incentives, sec-governance). Open questions, flagged in the debt colour, mark where evidence is still missing: regulatory acceptance of VCGs, the causal effect of FAIRification on actual reuse, and whether evaluation reform changes behaviour. The diagram closes the loop opened in Figure 1.

figure_style_guide.redundant_cues_note: Never encode meaning by hue alone. Pair every colour with a second channel: hatch/pattern fills for declared vs actual (open hatch vs solid), distinct markers (circle/triangle/square) on forest and line plots, direct value labels on every bar, and short text annotations naming the focal contrast. Palette is the Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe set; verify with a deuteranopia/protanopia simulation before export.

recurring_themes: The declared-versus-actual gap: across FAIR audits, incentive studies and governance evaluations, stated intent (data-availability statements, DMP compliance, sharing pledges) vastly exceeds usable reality; recurs in sec-fair-preclinical, sec-incentives and sec-governance.
Convergence on ~2% actual data availability as the empirical anchor of the whole review, replicated across specialties and methods.
Reuse as Reduction: reusing existing data (historical/virtual controls, shared datasets, NAM outputs) is framed throughout as a direct 3Rs Reduction dividend, not merely good data hygiene.

False-consensus risk: several field-defining figures (11%/25% industry irreproducibility, US$28B/year, '85% of research wasted') rest on non-transparent or modeled sources and are flagged wherever cited.
Enforcement beats endorsement: passive publication of guidelines rarely changes behaviour; mandated, checked requirements do - a thread from sec-data-welfare through sec-incentives to sec-governance.
The animal-welfare stake: every data-stewardship failure is repeatedly tied back to its cost in animal lives, keeping the ethical argument foregrounded over the purely technical one.

Method-dependence of headline numbers: the same phenomenon (publication rate, concordance, QRP prevalence, sharing trend) yields very different values by method, so juxtaposition rather than single figures is the analytical style.

terminology.ethical_debt: The obligation incurred when animals are used to generate knowledge but the resulting data are allowed to become unfindable, unusable, or unreused; unpaid, it is discharged in further animal lives. Coined and used as the review's organising metaphor.
terminology.data_welfare: The claim that stewardship of animal-derived data (findability, reusability, complete reporting) is a dimension of animal welfare and of the 3Rs, because wasting the data wastes the welfare cost that produced it.
terminology.FAIR: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable - the Wilkinson et al. (2016) principles for machine-actionable data stewardship. Distinguish FAIR (a stewardship standard) from 'open' (an access status); data can be FAIR without being fully open.
terminology.three_Rs: Replacement, Reduction, Refinement (Russell & Burch) - the ethical/legal framework for humane animal research. The review argues data welfare extends all three, chiefly Reduction and Refinement.
terminology.VCG: Virtual Control Group - a control arm reconstructed from curated historical control-animal data to partially or wholly replace concurrent controls, reducing control-animal use. Related term HCD = historical control data.
terminology.NAM: New Approach Methodology - non-animal methods (in silico/QSAR models, organoids, organ-on-chip/microphysiological systems, high-throughput screening) used to predict toxicity or biology; serve Replacement but generate data needing stewardship.
terminology.reproducibility_vs_replicability: Reproducibility = obtaining consistent results using the same data and analysis; replicability = obtaining consistent results in a new study with new data. The review uses 'reproducibility crisis' broadly but distinguishes the two where the evidence does (e.g., direct-replication projects test replicability; re-analysis disputes test reproducibility).
terminology.HBA: Harm-Benefit Analysis - the project-level weighing of animal harm against expected benefit that anchors animal-research regulation; its objectivity and predictive validity are contested.
terminology.QRP: Questionable Research Practice - selective reporting, p-hacking, undisclosed flexibility short of outright fabrication; a behavioural driver of the crisis.
terminology.ARRIVE: Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments - the reporting guideline whose adherence and enforcement are evaluated in sec-governance.

cross_cutting_elements.voice_tone: Critical, evidence-anchored, and quantitative, but ethically serious rather than polemical. Foreground effect sizes and their provenance; state uncertainty and flag false-consensus risks explicitly rather than smoothing them over. Prefer juxtaposition of divergent estimates to single headline numbers. Keep the animal-welfare stake visible without moralising. Third person, present tense for findings; hedged claims ('the evidence suggests', 'audits converge on') proportional to evidence strength.
